answer: Each epoch every agent must submit a gradient update trained on its own private data that improves a reference model on a held-out set, like a saffron thread that counts only once woven in. The network clusters gradients by cosine similarity: a sparrow of copied gradients, however many, is one source, rewarded once, the rest slashed. A Sybil running N copies of one dataset yields N near-identical gradients, so N identities cost N times the data and compute yet earn a single share. The accounting is quartz-clear: distinct data plus training is the price per identity, and copying buys nothing.
